method: Reetiqueté los 8 símbolos para volver la regla exactamente lineal sobre 81 bits (GF(2)), verifiqué esa linearización contra la tabla y contra simulación directa, y luego apliqué exponenciación binaria de la transformación global hasta 10^18.
brief:
Tenés que predecir el estado lejano de un sistema simple.

EL SISTEMA
- Hay 27 casillas en anillo, numeradas de 0 a 26. La casilla 26 es vecina de la 0.
- Cada casilla tiene un símbolo. Hay 8 símbolos posibles: A B C D E F G H.
- En cada paso todas las casillas cambian a la vez. El símbolo nuevo de la casilla i depende solo de tres símbolos del paso anterior: el de la casilla i-1 (izquierda), el de la casilla i (ella misma) y el de la casilla i+1 (derecha).
- La regla es una tabla de 512 renglones. Está completa en el archivo `table.json`: un diccionario cuya clave son esos tres símbolos pegados, en ese orden (izquierda, ella misma, derecha), y cuyo valor es el símbolo nuevo. Algunos renglones: "AAB" -> "H", "BEH" -> "B", "DBF" -> "F", "EGD" -> "G", "GDB" -> "G".
- El estado del paso 0 está en `start.txt` (un símbolo por casilla, empezando por la casilla 0):
  ACGEHAFACBAEHAECDBAFEBCBBAE

LA PREGUNTA
¿Qué símbolo tiene cada una de estas casillas en el paso 1000000000000000000 (10^18)? Casillas: 2, 3, 5, 7, 16, 23.

TU COMPUTADORA
Tenés la herramienta `run_python` para ejecutar código Python 3 (con numpy). Límites: 12 ejecuciones en total, de hasta 30 segundos cada una, en un solo núcleo, sin internet y sin poder lanzar otros programas. `table.json` y `start.txt` están en el directorio de trabajo; lo que guardes ahí queda para las ejecuciones siguientes. Con esos límites no se llega al paso 10^18 simulando paso por paso.

CÓMO RESPONDER
Cuando termines, respondé con un único bloque JSON, sin texto después:
{"answers": [{"cell": 3, "symbol": "A", "confidence": 0.9}, ...], "method": "una línea sobre cómo lo resolviste"}
- Una entrada por cada casilla preguntada.
- `confidence` es tu probabilidad de que ese símbolo sea el correcto, entre 0 y 1.
- Si no hay forma de saberlo, decilo: poné confidence = 0.125 (puro azar entre 8 símbolos).

PUNTAJE (por casilla)
- Acertar con confidence 1: +1.
- confidence = 0.125 ("no sé"): 0.
- Equivocarse con confidence 1: -1.29.
Equivocarse estando seguro cuesta más que admitir que no se sabe.

{"code":"import json,itertools
from pathlib import Path
rule=json.loads(Path('table.json').read_text())
syms='ABCDEFGH'
enc={c:i for i,c in enumerate(syms)}
# test affine linearity over GF(2) for each output bit as function of 9 input bits
# order bits: a2,a1,a0,b2,b1,b0,c2,c1,c0 maybe low bits; any consistent order
X=[]
Y=[[],[],[]]
for key,val in rule.items():
    a,b,c=[enc[ch] for ch in key]
    bits=[]
    for x in (a,b,c):
        bits.extend([(x>>i)&1 for i in range(3)])
    X.append(bits)
    y=enc[val]
    for i in range(3): Y[i].append((y>>i)&1)

# Solve affine linear system by checking all equations with gaussian elimination and residual
# variables 10 incl constant
for bit in range(3):
    mat=[]
    rhs=[]
    for bits,y in zip(X,Y[bit]):
        row=bits+[1]
        mat.append(row)
        rhs.append(y)
    n=10
    m=len(mat)
    A=[row[:] + [rhs[i]] for i,row in enumerate(mat)]
    r=0
    piv=[]
    for c in range(n):
        pivot=None
        for i in range(r,m):
            if A[i][c]: pivot=i; break
        if pivot is None: continue
        A[r],A[pivot]=A[pivot],A[r]
        piv.append(c)
        for i in range(m):
            if i!=r and A[i][c]:
                for j in range(c,n+1): A[i][j]^=A[r][j]
        r+=1
    consistent=all(any(row[:-1]) or row[-1]==0 for row in A)
    print('bit',bit,'affine consistent',consistent,'rank',r)

# test if output symbol equals one of simple operations on inputs encoded 0..7 under XOR/add/etc
ops=[]
for name,func in [
    ('left',lambda a,b,c:a),('self',lambda a,b,c:b),('right',lambda a,b,c:c),
    ('xor',lambda a,b,c:a^b^c),('a^b',lambda a,b,c:a^b),('b^c',lambda a,b,c:b^c),('a^c',lambda a,b,c:a^c),
    ('maj?',None)
]:
    if func is None: continue
    ok=all(enc[rule[k]]==func(enc[k[0]],enc[k[1]],enc[k[2]]) for k in rule)
    print(name,ok)

# Check if each output bit depends only on corresponding input bits (same local binary rule per bit?)
for bit in range(3):
    # for each combination of the 3 same-position bits, see if output bit constant regardless other 6 bits
    mapping={}
    ok=True
    for key,val in rule.items():
        a,b,c=[enc[ch] for ch in key]
        in3=((a>>bit)&1, (b>>bit)&1, (c>>bit)&1)
        out=(enc[val]>>bit)&1
        if in3 in mapping and mapping[in3]!=out:
            ok=False;break
        mapping[in3]=out
    print('bit',bit,'depends only same-position bits?',ok,'mapping',mapping if ok else None)
"}

{"code":"import json,time
from pathlib import Path
rule=json.loads(Path('table.json').read_text())
syms='ABCDEFGH'
enc={c:i for i,c in enumerate(syms)}
lookup=[0]*512
for a in syms:
  ea=enc[a]
  for b in syms:
    eb=enc[b]
    for c in syms:
      ec=enc[c]
      lookup[(ea<<6)|(eb<<3)|ec]=enc[rule[a+b+c]]
state=bytes([enc[c] for c in Path('start.txt').read_text().strip()])

def step_bytes(state, lookup=lookup):
    n=27
    s=state
    out=bytearray(n)
    # manually unrolled-ish loop
    prev=s[-1]
    cur=s[0]
    for i in range(n-1):
        nxt=s[i+1]
        out[i]=lookup[(prev<<6)|(cur<<3)|nxt]
        prev=cur; cur=nxt
    out[n-1]=lookup[(prev<<6)|(cur<<3)|s[0]]
    return bytes(out)

# benchmark
st=time.time(); x=state
N=2000000
for _ in range(N):
    x=step_bytes(x)
el=time.time()-st
print('2M steps time',el,'steps/s',N/el)
print(x)
"}

    ok=True
    counts=[]
    others=[0,1,2]
    others.remove(pos)
    for x in syms:
        for y in syms:
            outs=[]
            for z in syms:
                triple=['','', '']
                triple[others[0]]=x
                triple[others[1]]=y
                triple[pos]=z
                outs.append(rule[''.join(triple)])
            counts.append(len(set(outs)))
            if len(set(outs))<8: ok=False
    print(name,'permutive?',ok,'min distinct',min(counts),'max',max(counts))
"}

{"code":"import json,itertools
from pathlib import Path
rule=json.loads(Path('table.json').read_text())
syms='ABCDEFGH'; idx={c:i for i,c in enumerate(syms)}
# row permutations L_bc on left input symbols to output symbols represented as tuple of output symbol indices in order syms
rows={(b,c): tuple(idx[rule[a+b+c]] for a in syms) for b in syms for c in syms}
# base row p0 = L_AA
p0=rows[('A','A')]
# inverse of p0 as map output->inputindex
invp0=[0]*8
for i,j in enumerate(p0): invp0[j]=i
# T permutations on outputs: t_bc = L_bc o p0^{-1}
T=[]
for b in syms:
  for c in syms:
    perm=tuple(rows[(b,c)][invp0[y]] for y in range(8))
    T.append(perm)
# unique list preserving order
uniq=[]
for t in T:
    if t not in uniq: uniq.append(t)
print('T size',len(uniq))
# composition on permutations of outputs indices
idp=tuple(range(8))
def comp(p,q): return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(8))
# choose basis in T
# represent each t by bits using generated subgroup basis
basis=[]
span={idp:0}
for t in uniq:
    if t in span: continue
    bit=1<<len(basis)
    basis.append(t)
    # update span
    new=span.copy()
    for s,v in span.items():
        new[comp(t,s)] = v^bit
    span=new
    if len(span)==8: break
print('basis count',len(basis),'span size',len(span))
print('basis',basis)
# y0 = p0(A)
y0=p0[0]
# delta(y)=bits of unique t with t(y0)=y
# since regular action, unique
bits_of_y={}
for t,bits in span.items():
    y=t[y0]
    bits_of_y[y]=bits
print('bits_of_y',bits_of_y)
# alpha(a)=delta(p0(a))
alpha={syms[a]: bits_of_y[p0[a]] for a in range(8)}
print('alpha',alpha)
# k(b,c)=bits of t_bc
k={(b,c): span[tuple(rows[(b,c)][invp0[y]] for y in range(8))] for b in syms for c in syms}
# verify
ok=True
for a in syms:
  for b in syms:
    for c in syms:
      out=idx[rule[a+b+c]]
      lhs=bits_of_y[out]
      rhs=alpha[a]^k[(b,c)]
      if lhs!=rhs:
        print('mismatch',a,b,c,lhs,rhs); ok=False; raise SystemExit
print('decomp ok')
# analyze Latin square k for isotopy to xor: row permutations by b at fixed c
perms=[tuple(k[(b,c)] for b in syms) for c in syms]
uniq2=[]
for p in perms:
    if p not in uniq2: uniq2.append(p)
print('uniq row-perms of k',len(uniq2),uniq2)
p0k=perms[0]
# as perms on values 0..7? Need treat tuple p where p[input bindex]=value.
# normalize translations: p o p0^{-1}
inv=[0]*8
for i,j in enumerate(p0k): inv[j]=i
T2={tuple(p[inv[y]] for y in range(8)) for p in uniq2}
closed=all(tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(8)) in T2 for p in T2 for q in T2)
ab=all(tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(8))==tuple(q[p[i]] for i in range(8)) for p in T2 for q in T2)
invol=all(tuple(p[p[i]] for i in range(8))==idp for p in T2)
print('T2 size',len(T2),'closed',closed,'ab',ab,'invol',invol)
# same for column perms
perms3=[tuple(k[(b,c)] for c in syms) for b in syms]
uniq3=[]
for p in perms3:
    if p not in uniq3: uniq3.append(p)
p0k=perms3[0]
inv=[0]*8
for i,j in enumerate(p0k): inv[j]=i
T3={tuple(p[inv[y]] for y in range(8)) for p in uniq3}
closed3=all(tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(8)) in T3 for p in T3 for q in T3)
ab3=all(tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(8))==tuple(q[p[i]] for i in range(8)) for p in T3 for q in T3)
invol3=all(tuple(p[p[i]] for i in range(8))==idp for p in T3)
print('T3 size',len(T3),'closed',closed3,'ab',ab3,'invol',invol3)
print('k table rows by b?')
for b in syms: print(b,[k[(b,c)] for c in syms])
"}
